title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after Fargo, North Dakota police wrongly charged her with bank theft. She faced four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud. Lipps was released on Christmas Eve with no way home.

Lipps has now filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million from the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck. She alleges police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and social media photo without further investigation. The lawsuit says she lost her home, car, and belongings, and was denied medications and dentures while jailed. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The case will proceed in federal court.
